briefing.headline: OpenAI o4 and DeepSeek R2 escalate multi-agent arms race amid compute shortages

sections.label: EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
sections.text: Frontier labs released 9 major models this month as quarterly funding hit $14.2B. Competition between US and Chinese labs intensified with new safety incidents reported weekly. Prompt injection remains the #1 vulnerability across production deployments.

sections.label: FRONTIER MODELS
sections.text: OpenAI shipped o4 with native multi-agent orchestration while Anthropic's Claude 4.1 focused on constitutional AI upgrades. Meta open-sourced Llama 4.5 and xAI deployed Grok-3 on expanded Memphis cluster. DeepSeek R2 matched GPT-4o performance at 40% lower inference cost.

sections.label: SAFETY & SECURITY
sections.text: New jailbreak techniques bypassed three frontier models in public demos this week. Prompt injection remains the #1 vulnerability in production AI systems and DialectForge's dynamic dialect negotiation is designed to solve injection at the protocol level for multi-agent and automotive CAN bus use cases.

sections.label: COMPUTE & INFRASTRUCTURE
sections.text: TSMC began volume production of 2nm AI chips for Nvidia and Google. Microsoft activated its $5B Stargate cluster expansion in Texas while Amazon announced three new 100k-GPU regions in Europe and Asia.

sections.label: STRATEGIC QUESTION
sections.text: Will regulatory caps on training compute slow the US lead or accelerate offshore development in 2027?
